title: How AI could change the skills you need
titleChinese: 人工智能将如何改变你所需掌握的技能
paragraphs: Are you worried that you can't keep up with AI? Current artificial intelligence systems can do many tasks much quicker than we can. Does this mean that machines will put us out of work?

Rather than replace our jobs, it may be more likely that AI will transform the way we work. Previous waves of mechanisation and automation did not cause lasting effects to employment rates. However, the skills valued by the economy could change. Research from Goldman Sachs shows some evidence that AI has affected the US job market differently in different sectors. Being adaptable and understanding how AI and humans can best work together in the industry that you work in is likely to become very important.

Humans and artificial intelligence have different strengths. AI systems are naturally best suited to tasks that are repetitive, involve data and that are very large. Humans usually perform best when skills and qualities such as leadership, empathy and judgement are required. Recent research from MIT's Sloan School of Management identified which tasks were best done by humans, and which were best done by AI. They found that where humans were better, working together with AI boosted performance above that of humans working alone. Creative tasks could be an area where this collaboration is particularly productive. Professor David Stilwell from Cambridge University highlights that AI's creativity is currently at a similar level to an average human. Other research shows that using ideas generated by AI, even bad ones, helps humans to come up with better ideas more quickly.

Companies need to look at their workflows and processes to see where using AI alone or in collaboration with humans can be more efficient. They can then decide how best to integrate AI into their workflow. Employees should try to learn how best to use AI to support themselves. Being able to do this effectively will help lead to career success.
chineseParagraphs: 你是否担心自己跟不上人工智能的发展？当前的人工智能系统处理许多任务的速度远超我们人类。这是否意味着机器将让我们失业？
人工智能或许更可能改变我们的工作方式，而非直接取代我们的工作。以往的机械化和自动化浪潮并未对就业率造成持久影响。然而，经济所看重的技能可能会发生变化。高盛的研究展示了一些相关证据，人工智能对美国就业市场的影响因行业而异。具备适应能力，并理解在你所处的行业中，人工智能与人类如何实现最佳协作，这一点可能会变得至关重要。

人类与人工智能各有其优势。人工智能系统天然最适合处理那些重复性的、涉及大量数据的任务。而人类通常在需要领导力、同理心和判断力等技能与品质时表现最佳。麻省理工学院斯隆管理学院的最新研究明确了哪些任务最适合由人类完成，哪些最适合由人工智能完成。他们发现，在人类擅长的领域，与人工智能协作能提升绩效，使其优于人类单独工作。创意性任务可能是这种人机协作尤其富有成效的领域。剑桥大学的戴维·斯蒂尔韦尔教授指出，人工智能当前的创造力水平与普通人类相当。另有研究表明，即使使用人工智能生成的平庸甚至糟糕的点子，也能帮助人类更快地产生更好的想法。
公司需要审视其工作流程和工序，以确定在哪些环节单独使用人工智能或与人类协作能提高效率。然后，然后他们可以决定如何最好地将人工智能整合到工作流程中。员工应努力学习如何最好地利用人工智能来支持自身工作。能够有效地做到这一点，将有助于取得职业成功。

vocabulary.translation: 新软件显著改善了我们的工作流程。

vocabulary.entry: process /ˈprəʊses/ n. 流程，步骤
vocabulary.example: The manufacturing process is highly automated.
vocabulary.translation: 生产过程高度自动化。

vocabulary.entry: efficient /ɪˈfɪʃnt/ adj. 高效的，有效率的
vocabulary.example: The new system is much more efficient than the old one.
vocabulary.translation: 新系统比旧系统高效得多。

vocabulary.definition: 使融入，整合到（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: integrate into /ˈɪntɪɡreɪt ɪntə/ phr. v. 使融入，整合到（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The school aims to integrate technology into all subjects.

vocabulary.example: Effective communication is key to career success.
vocabulary.translation: 有效沟通是职业成功的关键。

title: The city streets beneath our feet
titleChinese: 我们脚下深处的城市街道
paragraphs: Stand outside Chancery Lane Tube station in London and you'll probably notice the regular commuters, trendy cafes and the odd tourist. Look up and you'll see the Staple Inn, built in 1585, and one of the last remaining Tudor timber-framed facades in London. But deep below your feet, there's more history lurking.

Nestled between Furnival Street and Fulwood Place in this area of London are a network of tunnels even deeper than The London Underground. Built between 1940 and 1942, the tunnels were constructed as part of the war effort as an air-raid shelter, designed to protect civilians and soldiers from bombs dropped in the war. Later in World War Two, the tunnels were occupied by Special Operations Executive and are even believed to have been the inspiration behind Q branch in the James Bond novels. The tunnels are set to open to the public in the near future.

Somewhere that can never open to the public is a secret Victorian street in Bristol. Now considered too dangerous to enter, a local historian climbed down to the street in 1999. He hoped to find gas street lamps, sash window frames and Victorian fire grates frozen in time. Instead, he found thieves had stripped the street, and it was mostly full of rubbish, though some bricked-up shop windows remained. The row of shops was buried in 1879 when a railway was built, and the company raised the road level.

In Scotland, there is an even older piece of history under foot. Mary King's Close in the centre of Edinburgh is a hidden network of preserved streets and homes from the 1600s. Down under the Royal Mile, the alleyways were once bustling and open-air but also dark and rather smelly. Many Old Town Edinburgh streets in the 1600s consisted of high-tenement buildings where the rich occupied the top stories and the poor lived on the ground floors, which were often flooded with sewage. The streets on Mary King's Close were built over in the 1750s and only rediscovered in 2003 during an archaeological investigation. It's now a tourist attraction, so you can go down and see the streets for yourself.
So, when you're out and about in the city, admire what's above ground, but also consider the history that could be hiding beneath your feet.
chineseParagraphs: 站在伦敦钱塞里巷地铁站外，你很可能会注意到日常通勤者、时尚咖啡馆和偶尔出现的游客。抬头望去，你会看到建于1585年的斯台普尔旅馆，它是伦敦仅存的几座都铎时代木框架结构建筑之一。但在你脚下深处，还潜藏着更多历史。
位于伦敦这一区域的弗尼瓦尔街和弗尔伍德广场之间，隐藏着一个比伦敦地铁还要深的隧道网络。这些隧道建于1940年至1942年间，是二战期间作为防空洞而建造的，旨在保护平民和士兵免受战争空袭炸弹的伤害。二战后期，这些隧道由特别行动处接管，甚至被认为是詹姆斯·邦德小说中Q部门的灵感来源。这些隧道计划于不久的将来向公众开放。
在布里斯托尔，有一条永远无法向公众开放的隐秘维多利亚时代街道。由于现在被认为过于危险而无法进入，一位当地历史学家曾在1999年下到这条街道。他希望找到那些经久未变的煤气街灯、上下推拉窗框和维多利亚时代的壁炉栅。然而，他发现街道已被盗贼洗劫一空，大部分地方堆满了垃圾，尽管仍有一些用砖堵上的商店橱窗。这排商店在1879年因修建铁路而被掩埋，铁路公司当时抬高了路面。

在苏格兰，脚下还有更古老的历史遗迹。爱丁堡市中心的玛丽·金小巷是17世纪保存完好的街道和住宅构成的隐秘网络。在皇家大道地下，这些小巷曾经熙熙攘攘，是露天的，但也阴暗且气味难闻。17世纪爱丁堡老城的许多街道由高高的公寓楼组成，富人住在顶层，而穷人则住在常常被污水淹没的一楼。玛丽·金小巷的街道在18世纪50年代被新建筑覆盖，直到2003年的一次考古调查中才被重新发现。如今，它已成为一个旅游景点，你可以亲自下去一睹这些街道的风采。
所以，当你在城市里外出走动时，不妨欣赏地面上的风景，但也请想一想可能隐藏在你脚下的历史。

vocabulary.definition: 通勤者，上下班往返的人
vocabulary.entry: commuter /kəˈmjuːtə(r)/ n. 通勤者，上下班往返的人

vocabulary.translation: 火车上挤满了通勤者。

vocabulary.translation: 这个地区在年轻人中变得非常时髦。

vocabulary.entry: odd /ɒd/ adj. 偶尔的，零星的

vocabulary.translation: 他累了的时候会偶尔犯点错。

vocabulary.translation: 这所房子是都铎建筑的优秀范例。

vocabulary.entry: timber-framed /ˈtɪmbə freɪmd/ adj. 木框架结构的

vocabulary.translation: 这个村庄到处都是木框架结构的小屋。

vocabulary.entry: facade /fəˈsɑːd/ n. （建筑物的）正面，立面（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The building's facade was beautifully decorated.
vocabulary.translation: 建筑物的正面装饰得很漂亮。

vocabulary.entry: lurk /lɜːk/ v. 潜伏，潜藏（书面语）

vocabulary.translation: 危险潜藏于表面之下。

vocabulary.translation: 这个村庄坐落在一个山谷里。

vocabulary.example: During the war, people took cover in air-raid shelters.
vocabulary.translation: 战争期间，人们躲进防空洞。

vocabulary.translation: 这座城市有许多维多利亚时代的建筑。

vocabulary.entry: sash window /ˈsæʃ ˌwɪndəʊ/ n. 上下推拉窗（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The old house still has its original sash windows.
vocabulary.translation: 这栋老房子还保留着原来的上下推拉窗。

vocabulary.entry: frame /freɪm/ n. 框架，边框
vocabulary.example: The picture has a beautiful wooden frame.
vocabulary.translation: 这幅画有一个漂亮的木框。

vocabulary.entry: fire grate /ˈfaɪə ɡreɪt/ n. 壁炉炉栅（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The fire grate was filled with burning coals.
vocabulary.translation: 壁炉炉栅里装满了燃烧的煤。

vocabulary.definition: 经久不变的，定格在时间中（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: frozen in time /ˌfrəʊzn ɪn ˈtaɪm/ phr. 经久不变的，定格在时间中（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The abandoned village was frozen in time.
vocabulary.translation: 这个被遗弃的村庄定格在时间中。

vocabulary.entry: strip /strɪp/ v. 洗劫，剥去（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The thieves stripped the house of all valuables.
vocabulary.translation: 盗贼洗劫了房子里所有值钱的东西。

vocabulary.entry: bricked-up /ˈbrɪkt ʌp/ adj. 用砖堵住的
vocabulary.example: The windows were bricked-up to prevent entry.
vocabulary.translation: 窗户用砖堵住了以防止进入。

vocabulary.entry: row /rəʊ/ n. 一排（建筑物）
vocabulary.example: There is a row of shops on the high street.
vocabulary.translation: 商业街上有一排商店。

vocabulary.entry: raise /reɪz/ v. 抬高，提升
vocabulary.example: The floor was raised to prevent flooding.
vocabulary.translation: 地板被抬高了以防洪水。

vocabulary.entry: close /kləʊz/ n. （苏格兰）小巷，死胡同
vocabulary.example: Mary King's Close is a famous historic site in Edinburgh.
vocabulary.translation: 玛丽·金小巷是爱丁堡著名的历史遗址。

vocabulary.entry: preserved /prɪˈzɜːvd/ adj. 保存完好的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The house is perfectly preserved.
vocabulary.translation: 这所房子保存得完好无损。

vocabulary.entry: alleyway /ˈæliweɪ/ n. 小巷，胡同
vocabulary.example: The alleyway was narrow and dark.
vocabulary.translation: 这条小巷又窄又暗。

vocabulary.definition: 熙熙攘攘的，热闹的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: bustling /ˈbʌslɪŋ/ adj. 熙熙攘攘的，热闹的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The market was bustling with shoppers.
vocabulary.translation: 市场上购物者熙熙攘攘。

vocabulary.entry: open-air /ˌəʊpən ˈeə(r)/ adj. 露天的，户外的
vocabulary.example: The concert was held in an open-air theatre.
vocabulary.translation: 音乐会在露天剧场举行。

vocabulary.definition: 公寓楼，出租屋（尤指苏格兰或美国）（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: tenement /ˈtenəmənt/ n. 公寓楼，出租屋（尤指苏格兰或美国）（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Many old tenement buildings have been renovated.
vocabulary.translation: 许多旧公寓楼已被翻新。

vocabulary.entry: occupy /ˈɒkjupaɪ/ v. 占据，占用（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The sofa occupies too much space in the room.
vocabulary.translation: 沙发在房间里占太多空间。

vocabulary.entry: storey /ˈstɔːri/ n. 楼层（英式）
vocabulary.example: They live in a flat on the third storey.
vocabulary.translation: 他们住在四楼的公寓里。

vocabulary.entry: sewage /ˈsuːɪdʒ/ n. 污水，污物（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The sewage system needs to be repaired.
vocabulary.translation: 污水系统需要维修。

vocabulary.definition: 考古的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: archaeological /ˌɑːkiəˈlɒdʒɪkl/ adj. 考古的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Archaeological remains were found at the site.
vocabulary.translation: 在该遗址发现了考古遗存。

vocabulary.entry: investigation /ɪnˌvestɪˈɡeɪʃn/ n. 调查，研究（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The police are conducting an investigation.
vocabulary.translation: 警方正在进行调查。

vocabulary.entry: tourist attraction /ˈtʊərɪst əˌtrækʃn/ n. 旅游景点（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The castle is a major tourist attraction.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城堡是一个主要的旅游景点。

vocabulary.definition: 外出走动，四处活动（口语，固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: out and about /ˌaʊt ənd əˈbaʊt/ phr. 外出走动，四处活动（口语，固定表达）
vocabulary.example: I've been out and about all day.
vocabulary.translation: 我一整天都在外面奔波。

vocabulary.entry: admire /ədˈmaɪə(r)/ v. 欣赏，钦佩
vocabulary.example: We stopped to admire the beautiful sunset.
vocabulary.translation: 我们停下来欣赏美丽的日落。

vocabulary.entry: beneath /bɪˈniːθ/ prep. 在……之下（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The ground beneath our feet was soft.
vocabulary.translation: 我们脚下的地面很软。

sentences.english: Stand outside Chancery Lane Tube station in London and you'll probably notice the regular commuters, trendy cafes and the odd tourist.
sentences.chinese: 站在伦敦钱塞里巷地铁站外，你很可能会注意到日常通勤者、时尚咖啡馆和偶尔出现的游客。

sentences.english: Look up and you'll see the Staple Inn, built in 1585, and one of the last remaining Tudor timber-framed facades in London.
sentences.chinese: 抬头望去，你会看到建于1585年的斯台普尔旅馆，它是伦敦仅存的几座都铎时代木框架结构建筑之一。

sentences.english: But deep below your feet, there's more history lurking.
sentences.chinese: 但在你脚下深处，还潜藏着更多历史。

sentences.english: Nestled between Furnival Street and Fulwood Place in this area of London are a network of tunnels even deeper than The London Underground.
sentences.chinese: 位于伦敦这一区域的弗尼瓦尔街和弗尔伍德广场之间，隐藏着一个比伦敦地铁还要深的隧道网络。

sentences.english: Built between 1940 and 1942, the tunnels were constructed as part of the war effort as an air-raid shelter, designed to protect civilians and soldiers from bombs dropped in the war.
sentences.chinese: 这些隧道建于1940年至1942年间，是二战期间作为防空洞而建造的，旨在保护平民和士兵免受战争空袭炸弹的伤害。

sentences.english: Later in World War Two, the tunnels were occupied by Special Operations Executive and are even believed to have been the inspiration behind Q branch in the James Bond novels.
sentences.chinese: 二战后期，这些隧道由特别行动处接管，甚至被认为是詹姆斯·邦德小说中Q部门的灵感来源。

sentences.english: The tunnels are set to open to the public in the near future.
sentences.chinese: 这些隧道计划于不久的将来向公众开放。

sentences.english: Somewhere that can never open to the public is a secret Victorian street in Bristol.
sentences.chinese: 在布里斯托尔，有一条永远无法向公众开放的隐秘维多利亚时代街道。

sentences.english: Now considered too dangerous to enter, a local historian climbed down to the street in 1999.
sentences.chinese: 由于现在被认为过于危险而无法进入，一位当地历史学家曾在1999年下到这条街道。

sentences.english: He hoped to find gas street lamps, sash window frames and Victorian fire grates frozen in time.
sentences.chinese: 他希望找到那些经久未变的煤气街灯、上下推拉窗框和维多利亚时代的壁炉栅。

sentences.english: Instead, he found thieves had stripped the street, and it was mostly full of rubbish, though some bricked-up shop windows remained.
sentences.chinese: 然而，他发现街道已被盗贼洗劫一空，大部分地方堆满了垃圾，尽管仍有一些用砖堵上的商店橱窗。

sentences.english: The row of shops was buried in 1879 when a railway was built, and the company raised the road level.
sentences.chinese: 这排商店在1879年因修建铁路而被掩埋，铁路公司当时抬高了路面。

sentences.english: In Scotland, there is an even older piece of history under foot.
sentences.chinese: 在苏格兰，脚下还有更古老的历史遗迹。

sentences.english: Mary King's Close in the centre of Edinburgh is a hidden network of preserved streets and homes from the 1600s.
sentences.chinese: 爱丁堡市中心的玛丽·金小巷是17世纪保存完好的街道和住宅构成的隐秘网络。

sentences.english: Down under the Royal Mile, the alleyways were once bustling and open-air but also dark and rather smelly.
sentences.chinese: 在皇家大道地下，这些小巷曾经熙熙攘攘，是露天的，但也阴暗且气味难闻。

sentences.english: Many Old Town Edinburgh streets in the 1600s consisted of high-tenement buildings where the rich occupied the top stories and the poor lived on the ground floors, which were often flooded with sewage.
sentences.chinese: 17世纪爱丁堡老城的许多街道由高高的公寓楼组成，富人住在顶层，而穷人则住在常常被污水淹没的一楼。

sentences.english: The streets on Mary King's Close were built over in the 1750s and only rediscovered in 2003 during an archaeological investigation.
sentences.chinese: 玛丽·金小巷的街道在18世纪50年代被新建筑覆盖，直到2003年的一次考古调查中才被重新发现。

sentences.english: It's now a tourist attraction, so you can go down and see the streets for yourself.
sentences.chinese: 如今，它已成为一个旅游景点，你可以亲自下去一睹这些街道的风采。

sentences.english: So, when you're out and about in the city, admire what's above ground, but also consider the history that could be hiding beneath your feet.
sentences.chinese: 所以，当你在城市里外出走动时，不妨欣赏地面上的风景，但也请想一想可能隐藏在你脚下的历史。

title: The cost of car dependency
titleChinese: 汽车依赖的代价
paragraphs: Driving: do we love it because it's quick and convenient, or is it just that we don't have a choice? Either way, commuting by car is becoming more common across the world. While this could mean that people are getting more mobility and freedom, could it have a cost?

As the number of cars on the road increases, so does congestion. As more people travel by car, more road space is used up. According to the OECD's International Transport Forum, the average person travelling in a car takes up five times as much road space as someone on a bus. This is made worse by the fact that, on average, today's cars are larger than those of the past. Tailbacks and other traffic jams in the UK could be costing £7.5 billion each year in wasted time.

It's not just gridlock and wasted time that's the problem. Car dependency has significant health impacts. Air pollution from diesel and petrol cars can cause health problems such as asthma and other respiratory illnesses. Road traffic accidents lead to injuries and fatalities. Additional to this are the long-term problems caused by sedentary lifestyles, leading to poor fitness and obesity. Road-building developments can also split communities, leading people to feel cut off. Where road transport dominates an area, people without access to a car can feel isolated.

Cities and countries are sometimes tempted to build new roads to reduce the potential for snarl-ups. However, some experts say that this can cause induced demand where increased road capacity leads to more people driving, and congestion is soon back to its previous level. The other side of this theory is that when road space allocation is taken away from private cars, often congestion won't get any worse. Authorities in some cities, such as Seoul and Utrecht, have demolished motorways, leaving natural features such as streams and rivers in their place. Making drivers pay more is an approach used in cities like London, or Singapore, where ten-year car ownership licenses can cost over £60,000. The increased costs can help reduce the number of cars on the road and make traffic flow faster.
chineseParagraphs: 开车：我们喜欢它是因为它快捷方便，还是仅仅因为我们别无选择？无论哪种方式，开车通勤在全球都变得越来越普遍。虽然这可能意味着人们获得了更多的流动性和自由，但这是否也会付出代价呢？
随着路上汽车数量的增加，交通拥堵也随之加剧。随着越来越多的人选择开车出行，占用的道路空间也越来越多。根据经合组织国际运输论坛的数据，开车的人平均占用的道路空间是公交乘客的五倍。而如今汽车平均比过去更大，这使情况更加糟糕。在英国，车辆长龙和其他交通堵塞每年造成的浪费时间成本可能高达75亿英镑。
问题不仅仅是交通大堵塞和浪费时间。对汽车的依赖对健康有重大影响。柴油和汽油车造成的空气污染会引发哮喘和其他呼吸系统疾病等健康问题。道路交通事故会导致伤亡。此外，久坐不动的生活方式还会导致长期问题，如体质下降和肥胖。道路建设开发也可能割裂社区，让人们感觉与世隔绝。在汽车交通占主导地位的地区，没有汽车的人会感到孤立。

城市和国家有时会试图修建新道路以减少拥堵的可能性。然而，一些专家表示，这可能会引发“诱导需求”，即道路容量增加导致更多人开车，拥堵很快会恢复到之前的水平。该理论的另一面是，当从私家车手中分配道路空间时，拥堵通常不会恶化。首尔和乌得勒支等城市的一些当局已经拆除了高速公路，取而代之的是溪流和河流等自然景观。让司机支付更多费用是伦敦或新加坡等城市采用的方法，在这些地方，十年的汽车拥有许可证可能花费超过6万英镑。增加的成本有助于减少道路上的汽车数量，并使交通流动更快。

vocabulary.definition: 流动性，移动能力（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: mobility /məʊˈbɪləti/ n. 流动性，移动能力（书面语）
vocabulary.example: A car gives you greater mobility and freedom.
vocabulary.translation: 汽车给你更大的行动自由和灵活性。

vocabulary.entry: congestion /kənˈdʒestʃən/ n. 拥塞，堵车（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The city is taking measures to reduce traffic congestion.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市正在采取措施减少交通拥堵。

vocabulary.entry: use up /ˌjuːz ˈʌp/ phr. v. 用完，耗尽（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: We've used up all the printer paper.
vocabulary.translation: 我们用完了所有的打印纸。

vocabulary.entry: tailback /ˈteɪlbæk/ n. （车辆）长龙，堵车队列（英式）
vocabulary.example: There was a two-mile tailback on the motorway.
vocabulary.translation: 高速公路上排起了两英里的车辆长龙。

vocabulary.definition: 交通大堵塞，僵局（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: gridlock /ˈɡrɪdlɒk/ n. 交通大堵塞，僵局（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The city centre was in gridlock during rush hour.
vocabulary.translation: 市中心在高峰时段交通完全堵塞。

vocabulary.entry: dependency /dɪˈpendənsi/ n. 依赖，依靠（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The country's dependency on oil imports is a concern.
vocabulary.translation: 该国对石油进口的依赖令人担忧。

vocabulary.entry: significant /sɪɡˈnɪfɪkənt/ adj. 显著的，重大的
vocabulary.example: There has been a significant improvement in her health.
vocabulary.translation: 她的健康状况有了显著改善。

vocabulary.entry: diesel /ˈdiːzl/ n. 柴油
vocabulary.example: Diesel engines are more polluting than petrol ones.
vocabulary.translation: 柴油发动机比汽油发动机污染更大。

vocabulary.entry: asthma /ˈæsmə/ n. 哮喘（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: She suffers from asthma and carries an inhaler.
vocabulary.translation: 她患有哮喘，随身携带吸入器。

vocabulary.definition: 呼吸的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: respiratory /rəˈspɪrətri/ adj. 呼吸的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Smoking can cause respiratory problems.
vocabulary.translation: 吸烟会导致呼吸系统问题。

vocabulary.definition: 死亡（事故中的），死亡者（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: fatality /fəˈtæləti/ n. 死亡（事故中的），死亡者（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The accident resulted in five fatalities.
vocabulary.translation: 这次事故造成五人死亡。

vocabulary.definition: 需要久坐的，惯于久坐的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: sedentary /ˈsedntri/ adj. 需要久坐的，惯于久坐的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: A sedentary lifestyle can lead to health problems.
vocabulary.translation: 久坐不动的生活方式会导致健康问题。

vocabulary.definition: 肥胖症（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: obesity /əʊˈbiːsəti/ n. 肥胖症（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Obesity is a growing health problem in many countries.
vocabulary.translation: 肥胖症在许多国家都是一个日益严重的健康问题。

vocabulary.entry: split /splɪt/ v. 分裂，使分离
vocabulary.example: The issue has split the community.
vocabulary.translation: 这个问题使社区分裂了。

vocabulary.entry: cut off /ˌkʌt ˈɒf/ phr. v. 使隔绝，切断（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The village was cut off by the flood.
vocabulary.translation: 洪水使这个村庄与外界隔绝了。

vocabulary.entry: dominate /ˈdɒmɪneɪt/ v. 支配，主宰
vocabulary.example: The industry is dominated by a few large companies.
vocabulary.translation: 该行业由几家大公司主导。

vocabulary.entry: isolated /ˈaɪsəleɪtɪd/ adj. 孤立的，孤独的
vocabulary.example: Elderly people can feel isolated without social contact.
vocabulary.translation: 没有社交联系的老年人会感到孤独。

vocabulary.definition: 交通堵塞，混乱（英式口语）
vocabulary.entry: snarl-up /ˈsnɑːl ʌp/ n. 交通堵塞，混乱（英式口语）
vocabulary.example: A broken-down lorry caused a snarl-up on the motorway.
vocabulary.translation: 一辆抛锚的卡车在高速公路上造成了交通堵塞。

vocabulary.definition: 诱导需求（经济学专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: induced demand /ɪnˌdjuːst dɪˈmɑːnd/ n. 诱导需求（经济学专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Building more roads often leads to induced demand.
vocabulary.translation: 修建更多道路往往会引发诱导需求。

vocabulary.entry: capacity /kəˈpæsəti/ n. 容量，能力
vocabulary.example: The theatre has a seating capacity of 800.
vocabulary.translation: 这家剧院有800个座位。

vocabulary.entry: allocation /ˌæləˈkeɪʃn/ n. 分配，配给（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The allocation of resources needs to be fair.
vocabulary.translation: 资源的分配需要公平。

vocabulary.entry: demolish /dɪˈmɒlɪʃ/ v. 拆除，拆毁（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The old factory was demolished last year.
vocabulary.translation: 旧工厂去年被拆除了。

vocabulary.entry: motorway /ˈməʊtəweɪ/ n. 高速公路（英式）
vocabulary.example: The motorway was closed due to an accident.
vocabulary.translation: 高速公路因事故关闭了。

vocabulary.entry: license /ˈlaɪsns/ n. 许可证，执照（英式：licence）
vocabulary.example: She passed her driving test and got her license.
vocabulary.translation: 她通过了驾驶考试并拿到了驾照。

vocabulary.entry: flow /fləʊ/ v. 流动，流通
vocabulary.example: Traffic flows more smoothly after the new road opened.
vocabulary.translation: 新路开通后交通更加顺畅了。

vocabulary.entry: commuting /kəˈmjuːtɪŋ/ n. 通勤
vocabulary.example: Commuting by train is often quicker than driving.
vocabulary.translation: 乘坐火车通勤通常比开车快。

vocabulary.entry: convenient /kənˈviːniənt/ adj. 方便的，便利的
vocabulary.example: The location of the hotel is very convenient.
vocabulary.translation: 这家酒店的位置非常方便。

sentences.english: Driving: do we love it because it's quick and convenient, or is it just that we don't have a choice?
sentences.chinese: 开车：我们喜欢它是因为它快捷方便，还是仅仅因为我们别无选择？

sentences.english: Either way, commuting by car is becoming more common across the world.
sentences.chinese: 无论哪种方式，开车通勤在全球都变得越来越普遍。

sentences.english: While this could mean that people are getting more mobility and freedom, could it have a cost?
sentences.chinese: 虽然这可能意味着人们获得了更多的流动性和自由，但这是否也会付出代价呢？

sentences.english: As the number of cars on the road increases, so does congestion.
sentences.chinese: 随着路上汽车数量的增加，交通拥堵也随之加剧。

sentences.english: As more people travel by car, more road space is used up.
sentences.chinese: 随着越来越多的人选择开车出行，占用的道路空间也越来越多。

sentences.english: According to the OECD's International Transport Forum, the average person travelling in a car takes up five times as much road space as someone on a bus.
sentences.chinese: 根据经合组织国际运输论坛的数据，开车的人平均占用的道路空间是公交乘客的五倍。

sentences.english: This is made worse by the fact that, on average, today's cars are larger than those of the past.
sentences.chinese: 而如今汽车平均比过去更大，这使情况更加糟糕。

sentences.english: Tailbacks and other traffic jams in the UK could be costing £7.5 billion each year in wasted time.
sentences.chinese: 在英国，车辆长龙和其他交通堵塞每年造成的浪费时间成本可能高达75亿英镑。

sentences.english: It's not just gridlock and wasted time that's the problem.
sentences.chinese: 问题不仅仅是交通大堵塞和浪费时间。

sentences.english: Car dependency has significant health impacts.
sentences.chinese: 对汽车的依赖对健康有重大影响。

sentences.english: Air pollution from diesel and petrol cars can cause health problems such as asthma and other respiratory illnesses.
sentences.chinese: 柴油和汽油车造成的空气污染会引发哮喘和其他呼吸系统疾病等健康问题。

sentences.english: Road traffic accidents lead to injuries and fatalities.
sentences.chinese: 道路交通事故会导致伤亡。

sentences.english: Additional to this are the long-term problems caused by sedentary lifestyles, leading to poor fitness and obesity.
sentences.chinese: 此外，久坐不动的生活方式还会导致长期问题，如体质下降和肥胖。

sentences.english: Road-building developments can also split communities, leading people to feel cut off.
sentences.chinese: 道路建设开发也可能割裂社区，让人们感觉与世隔绝。

sentences.english: Where road transport dominates an area, people without access to a car can feel isolated.
sentences.chinese: 在汽车交通占主导地位的地区，没有汽车的人会感到孤立。

sentences.english: Cities and countries are sometimes tempted to build new roads to reduce the potential for snarl-ups.
sentences.chinese: 城市和国家有时会试图修建新道路以减少拥堵的可能性。

sentences.english: However, some experts say that this can cause induced demand where increased road capacity leads to more people driving, and congestion is soon back to its previous level.
sentences.chinese: 然而，一些专家表示，这可能会引发“诱导需求”，即道路容量增加导致更多人开车，拥堵很快会恢复到之前的水平。

sentences.english: The other side of this theory is that when road space allocation is taken away from private cars, often congestion won't get any worse.
sentences.chinese: 该理论的另一面是，当从私家车手中分配道路空间时，拥堵通常不会恶化。

sentences.english: Authorities in some cities, such as Seoul and Utrecht, have demolished motorways, leaving natural features such as streams and rivers in their place.
sentences.chinese: 首尔和乌得勒支等城市的一些当局已经拆除了高速公路，取而代之的是溪流和河流等自然景观。

sentences.english: Making drivers pay more is an approach used in cities like London, or Singapore, where ten-year car ownership licenses can cost over £60,000.
sentences.chinese: 让司机支付更多费用是伦敦或新加坡等城市采用的方法，在这些地方，十年的汽车拥有许可证可能花费超过6万英镑。

sentences.english: The increased costs can help reduce the number of cars on the road and make traffic flow faster.
sentences.chinese: 增加的成本有助于减少道路上的汽车数量，并使交通流动更快。

title: A new sport debuts at the Winter Olympics
titleChinese: 冬季奥林匹克运动会迎来新项目
paragraphs: How do you fancy being up a mountain at a height of around 3,000 metres with the temperature below zero, snow underfoot, variable weather, racing up and downhill? This is how some athletes will be competing in this year's winter Olympics.

Skimo, short for ski mountaineering, is the newest winter Olympic sport and will debut at the 2026 games in Milan-Cortina. It combines Alpine skiing with mountaineering and is a race against time where athletes are required to ascend and descend mountainous terrain using skis and other specialised equipment.

At the Olympics, there will be a relay event, and also a sprint competition which lasts just a few minutes. Athletes start in a steep uphill section using climbing skins. These are detachable grippy strips you attach to skis to prevent sliding. The athletes then rapidly transition to boot packing where skis are carried on a backpack as they run up an incline as fast as possible. There is then a technical downhill course full of tight turns and obstacles. Because of all the transitions, races can be won or lost in seconds depending on how smoothly the athletes can switch between modes.

One hopeful British qualifier, and a member of the GB Skimo squad, is Iain Innes. Despite the sport being included in the Olympics, which he says is great news, he doesn't think the events accurately represent ski mountaineering. "There is no element of mountaineering whatsoever, as the World Cups and Olympics are held on man-made slopes with berms and jumps and perfectly cut steps on the climbs", he told the British Mountaineering Council.

However, inclusion in the Olympics is a positive reflection of the sport's global growth and development. The International Ski Mountaineering Federation (ISMF) oversees the regulation and promotion of the sport and has established a World Cup circuit, as well as continental and World Championships, all of which have helped elevate the sport's standing. So, look out for this extreme sport this year and feel that adrenaline rush.
chineseParagraphs: 身处海拔约3000米的高山上，气温低于零度，脚下是积雪，天气变幻莫测，需要竞速上坡和下坡，你觉得怎么样？这就是一些运动员将在今年冬季奥运会上比赛的方式。
Skimo，即滑雪登山，是冬季奥运会的最新项目，将在2026年米兰-科尔蒂纳奥运会上首次亮相。它将高山滑雪与登山相结合，是一场与时间的赛跑，要求运动员使用滑雪板和其他专业装备在山区地形中上坡和下坡。
在奥运会上，将设有接力赛，以及仅持续几分钟的短距离竞速赛。运动员从陡峭的上坡路段开始，使用登山爬升辅助带。这些是可拆卸的防滑条，固定在滑雪板底部以防止滑倒。然后，运动员迅速转换为“boot packing”模式，即把滑雪板背在背包上，在斜坡上尽可能快地奔跑。接下来是充满急转弯和障碍物的技术性下坡赛道。由于所有这些转换，几秒钟就能决定比赛的胜负，取决于运动员在各模式间切换的流畅程度。
伊恩·英尼斯是英国滑雪登山队的一员，也是有希望获得奥运资格的选手之一。尽管他认为这项运动被纳入奥运会是个好消息，但他并不认为奥运项目能准确代表滑雪登山运动。他告诉英国登山理事会：“奥运和世界杯比赛都在人造斜坡上举行，设有护堤、跳跃点和攀登时切割完美的台阶，完全没有登山的元素。”
然而，被纳入奥运会是这项运动在全球成长和发展的正面反馈。国际滑雪登山联合会负责监督和推广这项运动，并建立了世界杯巡回赛以及洲际和世界锦标赛，所有这些都有助于提升这项运动的地位。所以，今年请关注这项极限运动，感受那份肾上腺素飙升的刺激。

title: Protecting your photos in a digital age
titleChinese: 如何在数字时代保管你的照片
paragraphs: "Say cheese!" That's what the person behind the camera might shout when they want you to smile for a photo. 2025 marked the 50th anniversary of digital photography. Steve Sasson, inventor of the first digital camera in 1975, told the BBC that it looked like a 'toaster with a lens' - not like the stylish cameras we see today! By 2005, more people were buying digital cameras than film cameras, which meant that a process which used to be slow and laborious, was now quick and easy.

The 2000s brought a snap-happy era, with people now able to take hundreds, even thousands of photos a year. But what they hadn't quite worked out yet was how to store them. Back then, people used a mishmash of hard drives, USB sticks and CDs - physical storage that was at risk of loss or theft. Later came online photo sharing via social media or free online photo galleries where you can upload photos to 'the cloud'. The problem is that if you chose just one of these options for photo storage, such as an old laptop that's now broken, or a social media website that no longer exists, you may have what's called a 'black hole' in your photographic record, with no photos of life in the noughties. So, what's the advice?

After losing an external hard drive with all her family photos, Cathi Nelson set up The Photo Managers, a company which helps people manage their photo collections. They say the best protection is their '3-2-1' rule of photo storage which involves having three copies of each photo, all in different places. One in the cloud, the second on a hard drive, and a third on a drive in a separate location, like someone else's house. If that sounds like too much work, just make sure your smartphone automatically uploads photos to the cloud, and then spare some time once a month to upload those to a hard drive. And if you're someone who takes hundreds of photos per month, it's also a good idea to regularly curate your camera roll - keep the best ones and delete the rest, so you feel more in control.

The key takeaway here is that each storage method has its pitfalls, so it's better to always use two methods over just one in order to have a backup. Online platforms can be shut down, and hard drives can be lost. Just make sure your memories don't fade into the digital black hole.
chineseParagraphs: 说茄子！”当相机后面的人想让你为拍照而微笑时，可能会喊这句话。2025年标志着数码摄影诞生50周年。1975年第一台数码相机的发明者史蒂夫·萨松告诉BBC，它看起来像一个“带镜头的烤面包机”，而不是我们今天看到的时尚相机！到2005年，购买数码相机的人数超过了购买胶片相机的人数，这意味着过去缓慢而费力的过程变得快捷方便。

21世纪初带来了一个热衷于拍照的时代，人们现在每年能拍摄数百甚至数千张照片。但他们当时还没完全搞明白的是如何存储这些照片。那时，人们使用硬盘、U盘和CD等各种物理存储设备，这些设备存在丢失或被盗的风险。后来，你可以将照片上传到“云端”进行在线照片分享，通过社交媒体或免费在线相册。问题是，如果你只选择了其中一种照片存储方式，比如一台现在坏掉的旧笔记本电脑，或者一个已经不复存在的社交媒体网站，你的照片记录中可能会出现所谓的“黑洞”，丢失了那个十年里的生活照片。那么，有什么建议呢？

在丢失了一个存有所有家庭照片的外置硬盘后，凯西·尼尔森创立了The Photo Managers，一家帮助人们管理照片收藏的公司。他们表示，最好的保护方法是他们的“3-2-1”照片存储规则，即每张照片保存三份副本，存放在不同的地方。一份在云端，第二份在硬盘上，第三份在另一个地点的驱动器上，比如别人家里。如果这听起来太麻烦，只需确保你的智能手机自动将照片上传到云端，然后每月抽时间将那些照片上传到硬盘一次。如果你是一个每月拍摄数百张照片的人，定期整理你的手机相册也是个好主意——保留最好的，删除其余的，这样你会更有一切尽在掌握的感觉。
这里的关键是，每种存储方式都有其隐患，所以最好总是使用两种方法而不是一种，以便有备份。在线平台可能关闭，硬盘可能丢失。务必确保你的记忆不会消失在数字黑洞中。

title: Why we procrastinate
titleChinese: 我们为什么会拖延
paragraphs: Is your house at its tidiest when you've got a deadline coming up? Do you have a list of jobs that you really need to do, but you really don't want to start doing? Procrastination can mean that we spend more time putting off a job than we'd ever actually spend completing it. Understanding why we do it might help us to understand how to stop doing it.

There are different reasons why people procrastinate. Some people avoid tasks if they can relate them to traumatic situations in their past. Sometimes we don't do certain tasks because we're swamped with other things. If people are unhappy about being asked to do something, they might put it off to feel like they are regaining some control. Another common reason for procrastination is just the worry that doing something will be unpleasant or that we will not be able to do it well enough to satisfy ourselves.

This last kind of procrastination can be a result of our mindset. People with a perfectionist mindset are likely to have a very rigid idea of what success in a task looks like. This is coupled with being anxious not to fail at that task. Psychology lecturer Annemiecke Apergis-Schoute points out that procrastination can be the result of a struggle between our brain's reward and threat systems. If the threat of failure or discomfort is greater than the potential reward from doing the task, we're likely to avoid it.

Cognitive flexibility could help us to avoid procrastinating. If we change the way that we think about a task, it can be easier to start working on it. If we can challenge our expectation of what succeeding could be, and how uncomfortable working on the task will be, it can seem less threatening. Breaking down tasks into small components also makes them less daunting as well as providing a feeling of achievement when each of these steps is completed. It can also be useful to consider what triggers procrastination for you. Having a better understanding of this can help you get things done.
chineseParagraphs: 当截止日期临近时，你的房子是不是变得最整洁？你是否有一堆真正需要做、但真心不想开始做的任务清单？拖延意味着我们花在推迟一项工作上的时间，可能比实际完成它所花的时间还要多。理解我们为什么会拖延，可能有助于我们明白如何停止拖延。
人们拖延的原因各不相同。如果某些任务能让他们联想到过去的创伤经历，有些人会回避这些任务。有时我们不完成某些任务是因为有很多其他事情要忙。如果人们对被要求做某事感到不满，他们可能会推迟，以此来感觉重新获得了一些控制权。拖延的另一个常见原因仅仅是担心做某事会不愉快，或者担心自己做得不够好，无法使自己满意。
这最后一种拖延可能源于我们的思维模式。具有完美主义心态的人可能对任务成功的标准抱有非常严格的想法。再加上对任务失败的焦虑。心理学讲师安妮米克·阿佩吉斯-肖特指出，拖延可能是我们大脑的奖励系统和威胁系统之间斗争的结果。如果失败或不舒适的威胁大于完成任务可能带来的回报，我们很可能会回避它。
认知灵活性可以帮助我们避免拖延。如果我们改变对任务的看法，着手去做就会更容易。如果我们能挑战自己对“成功”的预期，以及完成任务会多么“不舒适”的看法，任务看起来就不会那么有威胁性。将任务分解成小部分也能减少其令人生畏的程度，并在完成每一步时带来成就感。思考是什么触发了你的拖延也可能有所帮助。更好地理解这一点可以帮助你完成任务。

vocabulary.definition: 加上，与……相结合（固定表达）

vocabulary.definition: 认知灵活性（心理学专业术语）

vocabulary.definition: 完成事情，做事有效率（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: get things done /ˌɡet θɪŋz ˈdʌn/ phr. 完成事情，做事有效率（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: I need to focus and get things done today.
vocabulary.translation: 我今天需要集中精力把事情做好。

sentences.english: Is your house at its tidiest when you've got a deadline coming up?
sentences.chinese: 当截止日期临近时，你的房子是不是变得最整洁？

sentences.english: Do you have a list of jobs that you really need to do, but you really don't want to start doing?
sentences.chinese: 你是否有一堆真正需要做、但真心不想开始做的任务清单？

sentences.english: Procrastination can mean that we spend more time putting off a job than we'd ever actually spend completing it.
sentences.chinese: 拖延意味着我们花在推迟一项工作上的时间，可能比实际完成它所花的时间还要多。

sentences.english: Understanding why we do it might help us to understand how to stop doing it.
sentences.chinese: 理解我们为什么会拖延，可能有助于我们明白如何停止拖延。

sentences.english: There are different reasons why people procrastinate.
sentences.chinese: 人们拖延的原因各不相同。

sentences.english: Some people avoid tasks if they can relate them to traumatic situations in their past.
sentences.chinese: 如果某些任务能让他们联想到过去的创伤经历，有些人会回避这些任务。

sentences.english: Sometimes we don't do certain tasks because we're swamped with other things.
sentences.chinese: 有时我们不完成某些任务是因为有很多其他事情要忙。

sentences.english: If people are unhappy about being asked to do something, they might put it off to feel like they are regaining some control.
sentences.chinese: 如果人们对被要求做某事感到不满，他们可能会推迟，以此来感觉重新获得了一些控制权。

sentences.english: Another common reason for procrastination is just the worry that doing something will be unpleasant or that we will not be able to do it well enough to satisfy ourselves.
sentences.chinese: 拖延的另一个常见原因仅仅是担心做某事会不愉快，或者担心自己做得不够好，无法使自己满意。

sentences.english: This last kind of procrastination can be a result of our mindset.
sentences.chinese: 这最后一种拖延可能源于我们的思维模式。

sentences.english: People with a perfectionist mindset are likely to have a very rigid idea of what success in a task looks like.
sentences.chinese: 具有完美主义心态的人可能对任务成功的标准抱有非常严格的想法。

sentences.english: This is coupled with being anxious not to fail at that task.
sentences.chinese: 再加上对任务失败的焦虑。

sentences.english: Psychology lecturer Annemiecke Apergis-Schoute points out that procrastination can be the result of a struggle between our brain's reward and threat systems.
sentences.chinese: 心理学讲师安妮米克·阿佩吉斯-肖特指出，拖延可能是我们大脑的奖励系统和威胁系统之间斗争的结果。

sentences.english: If the threat of failure or discomfort is greater than the potential reward from doing the task, we're likely to avoid it.
sentences.chinese: 如果失败或不舒适的威胁大于完成任务可能带来的回报，我们很可能会回避它。

sentences.english: Cognitive flexibility could help us to avoid procrastinating.
sentences.chinese: 认知灵活性可以帮助我们避免拖延。

sentences.english: If we change the way that we think about a task, it can be easier to start working on it.
sentences.chinese: 如果我们改变对任务的看法，着手去做就会更容易。

sentences.english: If we can challenge our expectation of what succeeding could be, and how uncomfortable working on the task will be, it can seem less threatening.
sentences.chinese: 如果我们能挑战自己对“成功”的预期，以及完成任务会多么“不舒适”的看法，任务看起来就不会那么有威胁性。

sentences.english: Breaking down tasks into small components also makes them less daunting as well as providing a feeling of achievement when each of these steps is completed.
sentences.chinese: 将任务分解成小部分也能减少其令人生畏的程度，并在完成每一步时带来成就感。

sentences.english: It can also be useful to consider what triggers procrastination for you.
sentences.chinese: 思考是什么触发了你的拖延也可能有所帮助。

sentences.english: Having a better understanding of this can help you get things done.
sentences.chinese: 更好地理解这一点可以帮助你完成任务。

title: Why can we see faces everywhere?
titleChinese: 我们为什么总能随处看到一张脸？
paragraphs: Are you one of those people that sees faces in inanimate objects? Researchers at the National Institutes of Health have been trying to find out why this is. They have pinpointed a circuit in an evolutionarily ancient part of the brain. It's called the superior colliculus, and it helps us recognise facial features. It triggers movement of the eyes, turning of the head and enables us to detect faces.

This study helps us understand face pareidolia - the common psychological phenomenon where the brain perceives illusions of faces in objects, like seeing faces in the clouds, exteriors of houses or even in a slice of toast. A study carried out by Susan Wardle showed that the parts of the human brain that respond to faces are sensitive to the shapes of other objects, and that our visual system is optimised for detecting face-like structures.

To test whether the superior colliculus might help in face detection specifically, researchers assembled a collection of images, including faces, biological non-face objects, like hands and arms, and other miscellaneous items. They then showed these images to adult monkeys in their peripheral field and recorded neural responses in the superior colliculus. It was found that detection of faces was much faster and preferred by neurons. This explains how our brains do it.

But why do our brains do it? Well, it's mainly for survival. According to Dr Amanda Robinson at the University of Queensland, face pareidolia tells us a lot about how we recognise social cues. We can determine whether the person or thing looking at us is a threat because of their facial expression. Richard Krauzlis, senior author of the study, explained that "quick recognition is a key skill in humans and other primates", such as gorillas and chimps. Additionally, biologists have observed human facial recognition and neural developments among species ranging from dogs, sheep, birds and even some insects.

What we know about recognition of faces and expression can further inform research on conditions such as autism, where face detection and recognition are often impaired from early childhood. It also helps us understand why we think we saw a friendly face in the living room wallpaper.
chineseParagraphs: 你是那种会在无生命物体中看到人脸的人吗？美国国立卫生研究院的研究人员一直在试图找出原因。他们在从进化角度上非常古老的大脑部分区域精确定位了一个神经回路。它被称为上丘，帮助我们识别面部特征。它能触发眼球运动和头部转动，使我们能够检测到面孔。
这项研究有助于我们理解“人脸空想性错视”——一种常见的心理现象，即大脑在物体中感知到面孔的错觉，比如在云朵、房屋外观甚至一片吐司中看到人脸。苏珊·沃德尔进行的一项研究表明，人脑中负责回应面孔的区域对其他物体的形状也很敏感，并且我们的视觉系统经过优化，特别擅长检测类似面孔的结构。
为了测试上丘是否专门有助于面部检测，研究人员汇集了一系列图像，包括面孔、非面部的生物物体（如手和手臂）以及其他杂项物品。然后，他们将这些图像展示给成年猴子的外围视野，并记录上丘的神经反应。结果发现，神经元对面孔的检测要快得多，并且更倾向于检测面孔。这解释了我们的大脑是如何做到这一点的。

但我们的大脑为什么要这样做呢？嗯，主要是为了生存。据昆士兰大学的阿曼达·罗宾逊博士称，人脸空想性错视让我们了解到很多关于我们如何识别社交线索的信息。我们可以通过对方的面部表情来判断看着我们的人或物是否构成威胁。该研究的资深作者理查德·克劳兹利斯解释说，“快速识别是人类和其他灵长类动物（如大猩猩和黑猩猩）的一项关键技能。”此外，生物学家已经在狗、羊、鸟类甚至一些昆虫等物种中观察到了人类面部识别和神经发育的相关现象。
我们对面部识别和表情的认知可以进一步为自闭症等疾病的研究提供信息，自闭症患者的面部检测和识别的能力往往在童年早期就受到了损害。这也有助于我们理解为什么我们会觉得在客厅的墙纸上看到了一张友善的脸。

vocabulary.definition: 自闭症（专业术语，书面语）

vocabulary.translation: 早期干预可以帮助自闭症儿童。

vocabulary.entry: impaired /ɪmˈpeəd/ adj. 受损的，削弱的（书面语）

vocabulary.translation: 她为卧室选择了一款花卉壁纸。

sentences.english: Additionally, biologists have observed human facial recognition and neural developments among species ranging from dogs, sheep, birds and even some insects.
sentences.chinese: ”此外，生物学家已经在狗、羊、鸟类甚至一些昆虫等物种中观察到了人类面部识别和神经发育的相关现象。

sentences.english: What we know about recognition of faces and expression can further inform research on conditions such as autism, where face detection and recognition are often impaired from early childhood.

sentences.chinese: 这也有助于我们理解为什么我们会觉得在客厅的墙纸上看到了一张友善的脸。

title: Could humans have 33 senses?
titleChinese: 人类可能拥有 33 种感官吗？
paragraphs: Many of us grew up learning that humans have five senses: sight, hearing, taste, smell and touch - an idea dating back to the Ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle. But what if this list is incomplete? A sense is anything that can give your body information about the outside world, and some of these don't neatly fit into the traditional five. Modern scientists estimate there may be up to 33 different senses.

One sense that doesn't fit into one of the five boxes is proprioception. This is the sense of where your body parts are in space. Thanks to this sense, you can touch your nose with your eyes closed and walk around in the dark - you know where your legs are without looking. Then there's interoception which helps you sense things inside your body, like hunger and an increased heart rate. And don't take your sense of balance for granted. Balance relies on fluid in your inner ear to help you stay upright - this is what's called vestibular perception.

And the traditional five senses might not be as simple as they seem. Touch, the sense we associate with our hands and tactile sensations, also encompasses the sensation of pain, temperature and itch. To perceive the flavours in food and drink, you need a combination of taste, smell and touch to get the full experience - it's not all about the taste buds on your tongue! It is actually smell that contributes most of what we perceive as taste, so when a person suffers olfactory loss, they often can't enjoy food as much, according to a 2022 study published in Foods by Fjaeldstad and Smith.

Until recently, philosophers and scientists have studied each of the traditional five senses in isolation, but researchers at the University of London's Centre for the Study of the Senses have more of a multisensory approach - the senses are all working together to create an overall picture. In their 'Rethinking the Senses' project, they found that our perception of salt, sweet and sour flavours is reduced when there is white noise, but our perception of umami is not. This means that sound can enhance flavour, and that umami-rich foods like tomato juice might taste better on a plane.

So, perhaps humans are far more sensory creatures than Aristotle ever imagined. From balance and body awareness to the way sound can change flavour, our senses are constantly working together in ways we rarely notice.
chineseParagraphs: 我们中的许多人从小就知道人类有五种感官：视觉、听觉、味觉、嗅觉和触觉——这一观念可以追溯到古希腊哲学家亚里士多德。但如果这个列表不完整呢？感官是任何能让你的身体获取外部世界信息的东西，而其中一些并不能恰当地被归入传统的五种之中。现代科学家估计可能有多达33种不同的感官。
一种无法归入五类的感官是本体感觉。这是感知你身体各部分在空间中所处方位的感官。多亏了这种感觉，你可以闭着眼睛触摸到鼻子，在黑暗中行走——你不用看就知道你的腿在哪里。还有内感受，它能帮助你感知身体内部的情况，比如饥饿和心率加快。也不要认为你的平衡感是理所当然的。平衡依赖于内耳中的液体来帮助你保持直立——这就是所谓的前庭觉。

传统的五种感官可能并不像它们看起来那么简单。触觉，这种我们将手和触觉感受联系在一起的感官，也包括疼痛、温度和瘙痒的感觉。要感知食物和饮料的味道，你需要味觉、嗅觉和触觉的结合才能获得完整体验——这不仅仅关乎你舌头上的味蕾！实际上，我们感知为“味道”的大部分其实是嗅觉贡献的，所以当一个人失去嗅觉时，他们通常无法像以前那样享受食物，根据Fjaeldstad和Smith 2022年发表在《Foods》上的一项研究。
直到最近，哲学家和科学家们还一直孤立地研究传统的五种感官，但伦敦大学感官研究中心的 researchers 则采用了更多多感官的方法——各种感官共同协作，创造出整体画面。在他们的“重新思考感官”项目中，他们发现当存在白噪音时，我们对咸、甜、酸味的感知会减弱，但对鲜味的感知则不会。这意味着声音可以增强风味，而像番茄汁这样富含鲜味的食物在飞机上可能味道更好。
所以，也许人类远比亚里士多德所想象的更具感官性。从平衡和身体意识到声音改变风味的方式，我们的感官一直在以我们很少注意到的方式协同工作。

title: Shapes and colours of the Moon
titleChinese: 月亮的万千色相
paragraphs: You may have heard of the idiom 'once in a blue moon' to describe an event that doesn't happen often. But can the Moon really be blue? Our closest neighbour in this vast galaxy, the Moon, orbits the Earth like a natural satellite. Unlike many of the other planets in our Solar System, ours only has the one moon. If you flew to it, you would land on grey rocks. This is because the lunar surface is made from mostly magnesium, iron and other minerals of that colour. But, if you're lucky to have clear skies under the curtain of night, you may be able to admire its luminosity. You might even see that it seems to change shape and hue.

It's important to understand that the Moon reflects light from the Sun as it orbits the Earth, and that light bounces back to the Earth. The position of the Moon, Sun and the Earth determines how much of the Moon we see. The new Moon appears almost invisible in the sky as it is in total darkness. This is the opposite to the full Moon which is completely lit up. There are eight different phases to the lunar cycle between a full Moon and a new Moon, each lasting around 28 days. In fact, the word 'month' takes its root from 'Moon' because it was almost equal to the lunar phases.

The other phases include the crescent, quarter and gibbous phase. Crescent originates from the Latin verb 'crescere', meaning 'to increase', and so it is the phase just before and after a new Moon as it takes a concave shape. The quarter will show half of the Moon. 'Gibbous' gets its root from the Latin term 'gibbous' which applied to the Moon's convex shape. These shapes are determined by the adjectives 'waning', to get smaller, and 'waxing', to get bigger.

So now you know how we've named the shapes, what about those mesmerising colours? The light waves that reach our eyes can vary due to the Moon's position on the horizon and pollution. This is known as Rayleigh scattering. When the Moon is low, light travels through the densest part of the atmosphere and shorter waves of blue scatter away. This leaves only the red and orange light waves to reach us. A warmer atmosphere, as well as smoke from wildfire, may increase the scattering effect as well, making the Moon appear less dull in spring and summer. This is why it's more likely for you to look up and see a pink Moon in April, a golden Moon in May and July, and even a red coloured Moon in the month of June.
chineseParagraphs: 你可能听过习语千载难逢来形容不常发生的事件。但月亮真的会是蓝色的吗？月球是我们在这广阔银河系中最近的邻居，像一颗天然卫星一样绕地球运行。与我们太阳系中的许多其他行星不同，我们的地球只有这一颗卫星。如果你飞往月球，你会降落在灰色的岩石上。这是因为月球表面主要由镁、铁和其他灰色矿物质构成。但是，如果你幸运地在夜幕下拥有晴朗的天空，你或许能欣赏到它的光辉。你甚至可能看到它的形状和色调似乎在变化。
重要的是要知道，月球在绕地球运行时反射来自太阳的光，光再弹回地球。月球、太阳和地球的位置决定了我们看到月球的多少。新月在天空中几乎看不见，因为它完全处于黑暗中。这与完全被照亮的满月相反。从满月到新月之间，月相周期有八个不同的阶段，每个阶段持续大约28天。事实上，“月份”（month）这个词的词根就来自“月亮”（Moon），因为它几乎等同于月相周期。
其他月相包括蛾眉月、弦月和凸月。“Crescent”源自拉丁动词“crescere”，意为“增加”，因此它指的是新月前后呈现凹形的阶段。“弦月”会显示月亮的一半。“Gibbous”（凸月）的词根来自拉丁语“gibbous”，用于描述月亮凸起的形状。这些形状由形容词“waning”（渐亏，变小）和“waxing”（渐盈，变大）来确定。

现在你知道了我们如何命名月亮的形状，那那些迷人的色彩呢？到达我们眼睛的光波会因月亮在地平线上的位置和污染而变化。这被称为瑞利散射。当月亮位置较低时，光线穿过大气层最稠密的部分，较短的蓝色光波被散射掉。只留下红色和橙色的光波到达我们眼中。较温暖的大气层以及野火产生的烟雾也可能增加散射效应，使月亮在春季和夏季看起来不那么暗淡。这就是为什么你在四月更可能看到粉色的月亮，在五月和七月看到金色的月亮，甚至在六月看到红色的月亮。

vocabulary.translation: 他难得去看望父母一次。

vocabulary.entry: galaxy /ˈɡæləksi/ n. 星系（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: The Milky Way is the galaxy that contains our Solar System.
vocabulary.translation: 银河系是包含我们太阳系的星系。

vocabulary.entry: orbit /ˈɔːbɪt/ v. 绕……轨道运行（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The satellite orbits the Earth every 90 minutes.
vocabulary.translation: 这颗卫星每90分钟绕地球一周。

vocabulary.entry: satellite /ˈsætəlaɪt/ n. 卫星
vocabulary.example: The moon is a natural satellite of the Earth.
vocabulary.translation: 月球是地球的一颗天然卫星。

vocabulary.entry: Solar System /ˈsəʊlə ˌsɪstəm/ n. 太阳系（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: There are eight planets in our Solar System.
vocabulary.translation: 我们的太阳系中有八颗行星。

vocabulary.definition: 月球的，月亮的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: lunar /ˈluːnə(r)/ adj. 月球的，月亮的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The lunar surface is covered with craters.
vocabulary.translation: 月球表面布满了陨石坑。

vocabulary.entry: magnesium /mæɡˈniːziəm/ n. 镁（化学元素，专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Magnesium is an important mineral for the body.
vocabulary.translation: 镁是人体重要的矿物质。

vocabulary.entry: mineral /ˈmɪnərəl/ n. 矿物质
vocabulary.example: The water contains important minerals like calcium and magnesium.
vocabulary.translation: 这种水含有钙和镁等重要矿物质。

vocabulary.entry: luminosity /ˌluːmɪˈnɒsəti/ n. 发光性，亮度（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The luminosity of the stars was breathtaking.
vocabulary.translation: 星星的亮度令人叹为观止。

vocabulary.entry: hue /hjuː/ n. 色调，色度（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The room was decorated in hues of blue and green.
vocabulary.translation: 房间装饰成蓝色和绿色的色调。

vocabulary.entry: phase /feɪz/ n. 阶段，时期；（月相）
vocabulary.example: The project is in its final phase.
vocabulary.translation: 该项目正处于最后阶段。

vocabulary.entry: crescent /ˈkresnt/ n. 蛾眉月，新月形
vocabulary.example: The moon was a thin crescent in the sky.
vocabulary.translation: 天空中的月亮是一弯蛾眉月。

vocabulary.entry: originate /əˈrɪdʒɪneɪt/ v. 起源，发源（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The game is thought to have originated in Europe.
vocabulary.translation: 这种游戏被认为起源于欧洲。

vocabulary.entry: concave /ˈkɒnkeɪv/ adj. 凹的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The inside of the bowl is concave.
vocabulary.translation: 碗的内侧是凹的。

vocabulary.entry: convex /ˈkɒnveks/ adj. 凸的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The lens is convex on both sides.
vocabulary.translation: 这个镜片两面都是凸的。

vocabulary.entry: waning /ˈweɪnɪŋ/ adj. 渐亏的，衰退的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The moon was in its waning phase.
vocabulary.translation: 月亮正处于渐亏阶段。

vocabulary.entry: waxing /ˈwæksɪŋ/ adj. 渐盈的，增长的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The moon is waxing towards fullness.
vocabulary.translation: 月亮正朝着满月渐盈。

vocabulary.definition: 令人着迷的，引人入胜的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: mesmerising /ˈmezməraɪzɪŋ/ adj. 令人着迷的，引人入胜的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The view from the top was mesmerising.
vocabulary.translation: 山顶的景色令人着迷。

vocabulary.entry: horizon /həˈraɪzn/ n. 地平线
vocabulary.example: The sun sank below the horizon.
vocabulary.translation: 太阳落到了地平线以下。

vocabulary.entry: Rayleigh scattering /ˈreɪli ˈskætərɪŋ/ n. 瑞利散射（物理学术语）
vocabulary.example: Rayleigh scattering explains why the sky is blue.
vocabulary.translation: 瑞利散射解释了为什么天空是蓝色的。

vocabulary.entry: scatter /ˈskætə(r)/ v. 散开，分散（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The birds scattered when they heard the noise.
vocabulary.translation: 鸟儿听到声音后四处飞散。

vocabulary.entry: dense /dens/ adj. 密集的，浓密的
vocabulary.example: The forest was so dense that we could barely see the sky.
vocabulary.translation: 森林如此茂密，我们几乎看不到天空。

vocabulary.entry: atmosphere /ˈætməsfɪə(r)/ n. 大气，大气层
vocabulary.example: The spacecraft re-entered the Earth's atmosphere.
vocabulary.translation: 宇宙飞船重新进入了地球大气层。

vocabulary.entry: wildfire /ˈwaɪldfaɪə(r)/ n. 野火
vocabulary.example: The dry summer has increased the risk of wildfires.
vocabulary.translation: 干燥的夏季增加了发生野火的风险。

vocabulary.entry: dull /dʌl/ adj. 暗淡的，乏味的
vocabulary.example: The sky was dull and grey.
vocabulary.translation: 天空阴沉灰暗。

sentences.english: You may have heard of the idiom 'once in a blue moon' to describe an event that doesn't happen often.
sentences.chinese: 你可能听过习语千载难逢来形容不常发生的事件。

sentences.english: But can the Moon really be blue?
sentences.chinese: 但月亮真的会是蓝色的吗？

sentences.english: Our closest neighbour in this vast galaxy, the Moon, orbits the Earth like a natural satellite.
sentences.chinese: 月球是我们在这广阔银河系中最近的邻居，像一颗天然卫星一样绕地球运行。

sentences.english: Unlike many of the other planets in our Solar System, ours only has the one moon.
sentences.chinese: 与我们太阳系中的许多其他行星不同，我们的地球只有这一颗卫星。

sentences.english: If you flew to it, you would land on grey rocks.
sentences.chinese: 如果你飞往月球，你会降落在灰色的岩石上。

sentences.english: This is because the lunar surface is made from mostly magnesium, iron and other minerals of that colour.
sentences.chinese: 这是因为月球表面主要由镁、铁和其他灰色矿物质构成。

sentences.english: But, if you're lucky to have clear skies under the curtain of night, you may be able to admire its luminosity.
sentences.chinese: 但是，如果你幸运地在夜幕下拥有晴朗的天空，你或许能欣赏到它的光辉。

sentences.english: You might even see that it seems to change shape and hue.
sentences.chinese: 你甚至可能看到它的形状和色调似乎在变化。

sentences.english: It's important to understand that the Moon reflects light from the Sun as it orbits the Earth, and that light bounces back to the Earth.
sentences.chinese: 重要的是要知道，月球在绕地球运行时反射来自太阳的光，光再弹回地球。

sentences.english: The position of the Moon, Sun and the Earth determines how much of the Moon we see.
sentences.chinese: 月球、太阳和地球的位置决定了我们看到月球的多少。

sentences.english: The new Moon appears almost invisible in the sky as it is in total darkness.
sentences.chinese: 新月在天空中几乎看不见，因为它完全处于黑暗中。

sentences.english: This is the opposite to the full Moon which is completely lit up.
sentences.chinese: 这与完全被照亮的满月相反。

sentences.english: There are eight different phases to the lunar cycle between a full Moon and a new Moon, each lasting around 28 days.
sentences.chinese: 从满月到新月之间，月相周期有八个不同的阶段，每个阶段持续大约28天。

sentences.english: In fact, the word 'month' takes its root from 'Moon' because it was almost equal to the lunar phases.
sentences.chinese: 事实上，“月份”（month）这个词的词根就来自“月亮”（Moon），因为它几乎等同于月相周期。

sentences.english: The other phases include the crescent, quarter and gibbous phase.
sentences.chinese: 其他月相包括蛾眉月、弦月和凸月。

sentences.english: Crescent originates from the Latin verb 'crescere', meaning 'to increase', and so it is the phase just before and after a new Moon as it takes a concave shape.
sentences.chinese: “Crescent”源自拉丁动词“crescere”，意为“增加”，因此它指的是新月前后呈现凹形的阶段。

sentences.english: The quarter will show half of the Moon.
sentences.chinese: “弦月”会显示月亮的一半。

sentences.english: 'Gibbous' gets its root from the Latin term 'gibbous' which applied to the Moon's convex shape.
sentences.chinese: “Gibbous”（凸月）的词根来自拉丁语“gibbous”，用于描述月亮凸起的形状。

sentences.english: These shapes are determined by the adjectives 'waning', to get smaller, and 'waxing', to get bigger.
sentences.chinese: 这些形状由形容词“waning”（渐亏，变小）和“waxing”（渐盈，变大）来确定。

sentences.english: So now you know how we've named the shapes, what about those mesmerising colours?
sentences.chinese: 现在你知道了我们如何命名月亮的形状，那那些迷人的色彩呢？

sentences.english: The light waves that reach our eyes can vary due to the Moon's position on the horizon and pollution.
sentences.chinese: 到达我们眼睛的光波会因月亮在地平线上的位置和污染而变化。

sentences.english: This is known as Rayleigh scattering.
sentences.chinese: 这被称为瑞利散射。

sentences.english: When the Moon is low, light travels through the densest part of the atmosphere and shorter waves of blue scatter away.
sentences.chinese: 当月亮位置较低时，光线穿过大气层最稠密的部分，较短的蓝色光波被散射掉。

sentences.english: This leaves only the red and orange light waves to reach us.
sentences.chinese: 只留下红色和橙色的光波到达我们眼中。

sentences.english: A warmer atmosphere, as well as smoke from wildfire, may increase the scattering effect as well, making the Moon appear less dull in spring and summer.
sentences.chinese: 较温暖的大气层以及野火产生的烟雾也可能增加散射效应，使月亮在春季和夏季看起来不那么暗淡。

sentences.english: This is why it's more likely for you to look up and see a pink Moon in April, a golden Moon in May and July, and even a red coloured Moon in the month of June.
sentences.chinese: 这就是为什么你在四月更可能看到粉色的月亮，在五月和七月看到金色的月亮，甚至在六月看到红色的月亮。

title: Programmes for those not watching
titleChinese: 给不看屏幕的人设计的电视节目
paragraphs: OK, I'm not proud of it, but sometimes when I'm watching TV, I might not actually be watching. Sometimes I'm just more tempted by my phone. Be honest, do you do the same? If you do, then we're not alone, lots of us watch TV with our phones in our hands. How is TV changing to accommodate this?

Let's start by looking at the data. Studies have investigated different countries across the world and many of them reported that most people use their phone while watching TV. While the classic stereotype is that it's younger people who find it hard to put their phone down, the data actually shows that second-screening is common in most age groups under 55. Younger age groups are more likely to be looking at social media or food delivery apps, while older age groups prefer banking, e-commerce and travel.

How are producers dealing with this? A number of screenwriters have reported being told that they need to make programmes easier to follow for distracted viewers. Reports say that showrunners have asked for more exposition in dialogue, repetition of plot points and increased use of voice-over to make things clearer for those who aren't looking. Some critics and viewers have complained that this could be making series less complex and dialogue less natural.

Second screens are not the only reason that these things happen. Television drama writing developed from radio drama writing, which has to use dialogue to compensate for the lack of visuals. When books are adapted for TV or film, one challenge is how to tell the whole story with less narration. All this means that exposition has often been a feature of TV writing. As series became more prestigious and cinematic since the early 2000s, this clear signposting of plot points had become less common.

Of course, TV viewers and TV programmes are not all the same. There is space for both casual and more complex programmes. Maybe the most important thing is for us to remember when to put our phones down.
chineseParagraphs: 好吧，我对此并不自豪，但有时我看电视的时候，可能并没有真正在看。有时候手机对我更有吸引力。说实话，你也这样吗？如果你也这样，那我们并不孤单，我们很多人都是手里拿着手机看电视。电视节目为了适应这一现象正在发生怎样的变化呢？
让我们先看看数据。研究调查了全球不同国家，其中许多研究报告称，大多数人在看电视时会使用手机。虽然传统的刻板印象是年轻人很难放下手机，但数据显示，“第二屏幕”现象在55岁以下的大多数年龄段中都很常见。年轻群体更可能在看社交媒体或外卖软件，而年长群体则更喜欢使用银行、电商和旅游类应用。
制片人如何应对这种情况呢？许多编剧透露，他们被告知需要让节目更容易被分心的观众理解。有报道称，节目制作人要求在对话中加入更多解释性内容、重复情节要点，并增加画外音的使用，以便让那些不看屏幕的人也能明白。一些评论家和观众抱怨说，这可能会降低剧集的复杂性，并使对话显得不那么自然。
第二屏幕并不是这些现象发生的唯一原因。电视剧剧本创作源于广播剧剧本创作，广播剧必须依靠对话来弥补视觉画面的缺失。当书籍被改编成电视剧或电影时，挑战之一是如何用更少的旁白讲述完整的故事。所有这些都意味着，解释性内容一直是电视剧写作的一个特点。自21世纪初以来，随着剧集变得更加精品化和电影化，这种清晰标注情节转折点的做法变得不那么常见了。
当然，电视观众和电视节目并非都一样。既存在轻松休闲的节目，也有更复杂的节目。也许最重要的是，我们要记住什么时候该放下手机。

vocabulary.entry: tempt /tempt/ v. 诱惑，吸引
vocabulary.example: The offer of a free trip tempted him into booking.
vocabulary.translation: 免费旅行的提议吸引他预订了。

vocabulary.entry: accommodate /əˈkɒmədeɪt/ v. 适应，容纳（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The hotel can accommodate up to 500 guests.
vocabulary.translation: 这家酒店最多可容纳500位客人。

vocabulary.entry: stereotype /ˈsteriətaɪp/ n. 刻板印象，模式化观念
vocabulary.example: There are many stereotypes about people from different cultures.
vocabulary.translation: 关于不同文化背景的人存在许多刻板印象。

vocabulary.definition: 第二屏幕（观看电视时使用其他设备的行为）（口语，专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: second-screening /ˌsekənd ˈskriːnɪŋ/ n. 第二屏幕（观看电视时使用其他设备的行为）（口语，专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Second-screening has become a common habit for many TV viewers.
vocabulary.translation: 第二屏幕已经成为许多电视观众的常见习惯。

vocabulary.entry: e-commerce /ˈiː kɒmɜːs/ n. 电子商务（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: E-commerce has changed the way people shop.
vocabulary.translation: 电子商务改变了人们的购物方式。

vocabulary.entry: screenwriter /ˈskriːnraɪtə(r)/ n. 编剧（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The screenwriter won an award for the film's script.
vocabulary.translation: 这位编剧因电影剧本获奖。

vocabulary.entry: distracted /dɪˈstræktɪd/ adj. 分心的，注意力分散的
vocabulary.example: He seemed distracted during the meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 他在会议期间似乎心不在焉。

vocabulary.definition: 节目统筹（电视行业术语）
vocabulary.entry: showrunner /ˈʃəʊrʌnə(r)/ n. 节目统筹（电视行业术语）
vocabulary.example: The showrunner is responsible for the creative direction of the series.
vocabulary.translation: 节目统筹负责剧集的创意方向。

vocabulary.definition: 解释性内容（文学/戏剧术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: exposition /ˌekspəˈzɪʃn/ n. 解释性内容（文学/戏剧术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The play opens with a lot of exposition.
vocabulary.translation: 这部剧以大量解释性内容开场。

vocabulary.entry: dialogue /ˈdaɪəlɒɡ/ n. 对话，对白
vocabulary.example: The movie has some very funny dialogue.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影有一些非常有趣的对话。

vocabulary.entry: repetition /ˌrepəˈtɪʃn/ n. 重复（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Repetition is a useful learning tool.
vocabulary.translation: 重复是一种有用的学习工具。

vocabulary.definition: 情节转折点（文学/戏剧术语）
vocabulary.entry: plot point /ˈplɒt pɔɪnt/ n. 情节转折点（文学/戏剧术语）
vocabulary.example: The plot point at the end of the first act surprised everyone.
vocabulary.translation: 第一幕结尾的情节转折让所有人都感到惊讶。

vocabulary.entry: voice-over /ˈvɔɪs əʊvə(r)/ n. 画外音（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: The documentary used a voice-over to explain the images.
vocabulary.translation: 这部纪录片使用画外音来解释画面。

vocabulary.entry: critic /ˈkrɪtɪk/ n. 评论家，批评者
vocabulary.example: Critics of the plan say it's too expensive.
vocabulary.translation: 该计划的批评者说它太昂贵了。

vocabulary.entry: compensate /ˈkɒmpenseɪt/ v. 补偿，弥补（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Nothing can compensate for the loss of a loved one.
vocabulary.translation: 失去亲人是什么也弥补不了的。

vocabulary.definition: 视觉画面，视觉效果（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: visual /ˈvɪʒuəl/ n. 视觉画面，视觉效果（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The film has stunning visuals.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影有令人惊叹的视觉效果。

vocabulary.entry: adapt /əˈdæpt/ v. 改编，适应
vocabulary.example: The novel was adapted for television.
vocabulary.translation: 这部小说被改编成了电视剧。

vocabulary.entry: narration /nəˈreɪʃn/ n. 叙述，旁白（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The narration adds depth to the story.
vocabulary.translation: 旁白为故事增添了深度。

vocabulary.definition: 有声望的，受尊敬的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: prestigious /preˈstɪdʒəs/ adj. 有声望的，受尊敬的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: She graduated from a prestigious university.
vocabulary.translation: 她毕业于一所名牌大学。

vocabulary.definition: 电影的，电影制作的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: cinematic /ˌsɪnəˈmætɪk/ adj. 电影的，电影制作的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The film has a very cinematic quality.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影具有很强的电影质感。

vocabulary.entry: signposting /ˈsaɪnpəʊstɪŋ/ n. 清晰标注，指引（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Clear signposting of plot points helps viewers follow the story.
vocabulary.translation: 对情节转折点的清晰标注有助于观众跟上故事。

vocabulary.entry: casual /ˈkæʒuəl/ adj. 随意的，非正式的
vocabulary.example: He wore casual clothes to the party.
vocabulary.translation: 他穿着休闲装参加派对。

vocabulary.entry: put down /ˌpʊt ˈdaʊn/ phr. v. 放下（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Please put down your phones and listen to the teacher.
vocabulary.translation: 请放下手机，听老师讲课。

sentences.english: OK, I'm not proud of it, but sometimes when I'm watching TV, I might not actually be watching.
sentences.chinese: 好吧，我对此并不自豪，但有时我看电视的时候，可能并没有真正在看。

sentences.english: Sometimes I'm just more tempted by my phone.
sentences.chinese: 有时候手机对我更有吸引力。

sentences.english: Be honest, do you do the same?
sentences.chinese: 说实话，你也这样吗？

sentences.english: If you do, then we're not alone, lots of us watch TV with our phones in our hands.
sentences.chinese: 如果你也这样，那我们并不孤单，我们很多人都是手里拿着手机看电视。

sentences.english: How is TV changing to accommodate this?
sentences.chinese: 电视节目为了适应这一现象正在发生怎样的变化呢？

sentences.english: Let's start by looking at the data.
sentences.chinese: 让我们先看看数据。

sentences.english: Studies have investigated different countries across the world and many of them reported that most people use their phone while watching TV.
sentences.chinese: 研究调查了全球不同国家，其中许多研究报告称，大多数人在看电视时会使用手机。

sentences.english: While the classic stereotype is that it's younger people who find it hard to put their phone down, the data actually shows that second-screening is common in most age groups under 55.
sentences.chinese: 虽然传统的刻板印象是年轻人很难放下手机，但数据显示，“第二屏幕”现象在55岁以下的大多数年龄段中都很常见。

sentences.english: Younger age groups are more likely to be looking at social media or food delivery apps, while older age groups prefer banking, e-commerce and travel.
sentences.chinese: 年轻群体更可能在看社交媒体或外卖软件，而年长群体则更喜欢使用银行、电商和旅游类应用。

sentences.english: How are producers dealing with this?
sentences.chinese: 制片人如何应对这种情况呢？

sentences.english: A number of screenwriters have reported being told that they need to make programmes easier to follow for distracted viewers.
sentences.chinese: 许多编剧透露，他们被告知需要让节目更容易被分心的观众理解。

sentences.english: Reports say that showrunners have asked for more exposition in dialogue, repetition of plot points and increased use of voice-over to make things clearer for those who aren't looking.
sentences.chinese: 有报道称，节目制作人要求在对话中加入更多解释性内容、重复情节要点，并增加画外音的使用，以便让那些不看屏幕的人也能明白。

sentences.english: Some critics and viewers have complained that this could be making series less complex and dialogue less natural.
sentences.chinese: 一些评论家和观众抱怨说，这可能会降低剧集的复杂性，并使对话显得不那么自然。

sentences.english: Second screens are not the only reason that these things happen.
sentences.chinese: 第二屏幕并不是这些现象发生的唯一原因。

sentences.english: Television drama writing developed from radio drama writing, which has to use dialogue to compensate for the lack of visuals.
sentences.chinese: 电视剧剧本创作源于广播剧剧本创作，广播剧必须依靠对话来弥补视觉画面的缺失。

sentences.english: When books are adapted for TV or film, one challenge is how to tell the whole story with less narration.
sentences.chinese: 当书籍被改编成电视剧或电影时，挑战之一是如何用更少的旁白讲述完整的故事。

sentences.english: All this means that exposition has often been a feature of TV writing.
sentences.chinese: 所有这些都意味着，解释性内容一直是电视剧写作的一个特点。

sentences.english: As series became more prestigious and cinematic since the early 2000s, this clear signposting of plot points had become less common.
sentences.chinese: 自21世纪初以来，随着剧集变得更加精品化和电影化，这种清晰标注情节转折点的做法变得不那么常见了。

sentences.english: Of course, TV viewers and TV programmes are not all the same.
sentences.chinese: 当然，电视观众和电视节目并非都一样。

sentences.english: There is space for both casual and more complex programmes.
sentences.chinese: 既存在轻松休闲的节目，也有更复杂的节目。

sentences.english: Maybe the most important thing is for us to remember when to put our phones down.
sentences.chinese: 也许最重要的是，我们要记住什么时候该放下手机。

title: The healing power of singing
titleChinese: 歌唱的疗愈功效
paragraphs: From singing at concerts to singing 'Happy birthday'. Around the world, humans have been singing in unison for millennia. Some anthropologists even think our ancestors may have sung before they could speak. "Lullabies are sung to children, and then songs are sung at funerals", says Alex Street, from the Cambridge Institute for Music Therapy Research, who thinks that our positive response to music is no accident. Music is not only enjoyable, but beneficial for our health.

There is growing evidence that singing can energise us, improve immune function and increase feelings of happiness, according to 'A Review of the Physiological Effects and Mechanisms of Singing', published in 2018. It's thought that the repeated and controlled breathing that singing requires releases endorphins, which are chemicals released by the brain associated with pleasure and wellbeing. It may even provide a physical workout comparable to a brisk walk. And singing as part of a group or choir may have additional effects. Researchers in 'The icebreaker effect: singing mediates fast social bonding' found that singing together accelerated faster social cohesion among strangers.

Some studies have also found that regular musical activity can help to delay the onset of various neurological conditions such as Parkinson's disease and dementia. And it's not too late for those already living with such conditions. Cathy McGlynn is a music therapist based in Ireland who leads a choir of people with Parkinson's. The disease can lead to respiratory and vocal problems, both of which are benefited by singing practice. For those suffering with dementia, singing can enhance the type of memory which helps us recall names and specific personal experiences, according to a literature review on singing and cognitive health called 'A Song for the Mind'. Music therapist Grace Meadows watched as a woman with dementia got up out of her chair and started dancing at a musical performance. "It was the first time the carers had ever seen her move, unaided."

Music may not be a medicine in the traditional sense, but one thing seems clear: humans are wired for connection, and music helps to create it. So, if you're sceptical about the power of music, it may be time to change your tune.
chineseParagraphs: 从在音乐会唱歌到唱“生日快乐”歌。世界各地，人类齐声歌唱已有数千年历史。一些人类学家甚至认为我们的祖先在会说话之前可能就已经会唱歌了。“摇篮曲是唱给孩子的，而葬礼上也会唱歌，”剑桥音乐治疗研究所的亚历克斯·斯特里特说，他认为我们对音乐的积极反应并非偶然。音乐不仅令人愉悦，而且对我们的健康有益。
根据2018年发表的《歌唱的生理效应与机制回顾》，越来越多的证据表明，唱歌可以让我们充满活力，改善免疫功能，并增加幸福感。人们认为，唱歌所需的重复且有控制的呼吸会释放内啡肽，这是大脑释放的与愉悦和幸福相关的化学物质。它甚至可能提供相当于快走的身体锻炼。而作为团体或合唱团的一部分进行唱歌可能还有额外效果。《破冰效应：唱歌促进快速社会联系》的研究人员发现，一起唱歌能加速陌生人群之间的社会凝聚力。

一些研究还发现，定期的音乐活动有助于延缓帕金森病和痴呆等多种神经系统疾病的发作。对于已经患有这些疾病的人来说，现在开始也为时不晚。凯西·麦格林是爱尔兰的一名音乐治疗师，她领导着一个由帕金森病患者组成的合唱团。这种疾病可能导致呼吸和发声问题，而唱歌练习对这两方面都有益处。根据一篇关于唱歌和认知健康的文献综述《心灵的歌声》，对于痴呆症患者，唱歌可以增强那种帮助我们回忆名字和特定个人经历的记忆类型。音乐治疗师格蕾丝·梅多斯曾目睹一位患有痴呆症的女士在一场音乐表演中从椅子上站起来开始跳舞。“这是护理人员第一次看到她无需帮助就能自己活动。”
音乐可能不是传统意义上的药物，但有一点似乎很清楚：人类天生就为联系而生，而音乐有助于创造这种联系。所以，如果你对音乐的力量持怀疑态度，也许是时候改变你的看法了。

vocabulary.translation: 听到证据后他改变了看法。

title: Is there life on Venus?
titleChinese: 金星上有生命吗？
paragraphs: For years, astronomers have hypothesised about life beyond Earth, especially on the closest planet to Earth - Venus. Venus is often named the Earth's 'evil twin' because of its extremely hot temperature and greenhouse effect, which make it toxic and inhospitable. It is also similar in size, mass and rocky composition.

Though no organic molecules have been discovered on Venus, new findings from the Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) instrument on board NASA's Magellan spacecraft shows caves lurking beneath the surface. Researchers from Nature Communications add that these could offer us new ideas about the evolution of Venus - about how it might have possibly supported life in the past or could again in the future.

The caves suggest that lava tubes, otherwise known as pyroducts, could be prevalent. The search for pyroducts was challenging at first because the planet is shrouded in thick clouds of sulphur and carbon dioxide that not only contribute to the immense temperature but also block any view of the surface. However, the recent radar images suggest that a big pyroduct lies near Nyx Mons, a large volcano in the highlands of Venus's Bell Regio region.

In a 2026 study called 'Radar-based observation of a lava tube on Venus', it can be understood that, in the field of geoscience, volcanoes play an important role in the evolution of a planet. If we think about Earth billions of years ago, volcanoes released gases that helped form our oceans and our atmosphere. Volcanoes keep Earth warm, wet and habitable. So, we have evidence that there are many active volcanoes on Venus, but will we ever be able to live there?

Well, we would require an abundance of water, which is greatly lacking on Venus. But data gathered by the Venus Express orbiter, launched in 2005 by The European Space Agency, could hint toward the planet once having oceans. And though the clouds on Venus rain sulphuric acid, they could still support an exotic biochemistry that thrives in such conditions. There's also plenty of sunlight to serve as a power source for life.
chineseParagraphs: 多年来，天文学家们一直推测地球之外存在生命，尤其是在离地球最近的行星——金星上。金星常被称为地球的“邪恶双胞胎”，因为它拥有极高的温度和温室效应，使其具有毒性且不宜居。它的大小、质量和岩石成分也与地球相似。
虽然金星上尚未发现有机分子，但美国宇航局麦哲伦号飞船上的合成孔径雷达仪器的新发现表明，其地表下潜藏着洞穴。《自然·通讯》的研究人员补充说，这些洞穴可能为我们提供关于金星演化的新思路——关于它过去如何可能支持生命，或未来如何再次支持生命。
这些洞穴表明，熔岩管（也称为火山熔岩管）可能普遍存在。最初寻找火山熔岩管颇具挑战，因为这颗行星笼罩在厚厚的硫磺和二氧化碳云层中，这些云层不仅导致了极高的温度，也导致无法看到地表。然而，最近的雷达图像表明，在金星贝尔区高地的一座名为尼克斯山的大型火山附近，存在着一个大型火山熔岩管。
在2026年一项名为《基于雷达的金星熔岩管观测》的研究中，可以了解到，在地球科学领域，火山对行星的演化起着重要作用。回想数十亿年前的地球，火山释放的气体帮助形成了我们的海洋和大气层。火山使地球保持温暖、湿润和宜居。因此，我们有证据表明金星上存在许多活火山，但我们能住在那里吗？
嗯，我们需要大量的水，而金星上却极度缺水。但是，欧洲航天局于2005年发射的“金星快车”轨道器收集的数据可能暗示，这颗行星曾经有过海洋。尽管金星上的云层降下的是硫酸雨，但它们仍然可能支持在这种条件下繁衍生息的奇特生物化学过程。此外，还有充足的阳光可以作为生命的能量来源。

title: Is fibre the new fad? “
titleChinese: 膳食纤维热”：这只是一时的流行吗？
paragraphs: Since its discovery, food businesses have encouraged high-protein diets, according to research by the University of Oregon. Whether it's bars, shakes or even marshmallows, protein has always prevailed in conversations about health and fitness. Some people think that these kinds of diets are a fad because high-protein products appear on supermarket shelves often. However, these diets have slightly stagnated within the realm of wellness.

And that's because there's now another food group gaining popularity - fibre. Found in foods like fruits, vegetables, grains, nuts, seeds, and legumes, our enzymes can't break down fibre into nutrients to absorb like it would with other food groups. Instead, it passes through the digestive system, which helps regulate bowel movements. Multiple studies have shown that certain types of fibre can lower cholesterol, help manage blood sugar levels and improve general gut health. It can also help you feel fuller for longer as it takes more time to digest.

The World Health Organisation recommends that adults consume 25-35g of fibre a day. However, research by Tate & Lyle between the years of 2021 and 2022 shows that adults in many countries aren't even close to that benchmark. The National Institute of Health tells us that the fibre intake in women is less than men. Additionally, data from the World Health Organisation shows a trend that those living outside of cities, like villages and in the countryside, have lower fibre consumption in comparison to those who live in cities.

Studies have found that not eating enough fibre can have detrimental consequences on your health. Without it, your gut bacteria can't fight excess inflammation, provide energy, or manage your blood sugar levels or your mood. Physically, you're more likely to be constipated and to feel sluggish and tired.

So, what can you do? Well, dieticians say that you should eat five to eight portions of fruit and vegetables a day. Try throwing in a handful of cooked lentils or chickpeas into curries, soups or salads. You can also eat seeds, nuts and dried fruit as your snack between meals. It might feel fashionable to talk about fibre at the moment, but science suggests that we need it to be healthy. So, be careful to follow dieticians' advice and try to eat your fruits and veggies!
chineseParagraphs: 根据俄勒冈大学的研究，自发现以来，食品行业一直在推崇高蛋白饮食。无论是蛋白棒、奶昔还是棉花糖，蛋白质在健康和健身的讨论中总是占据主导地位。一些人认为这类饮食是一种“时尚”，因为高蛋白产品经常出现在超市货架上。然而，这些饮食在健康领域的热度略有停滞。
这是因为现在另一种食物类别正在兴起——膳食纤维。纤维存在于水果、蔬菜、谷物、坚果、种子和豆类等食物中，我们的酶无法像分解其他食物那样将纤维分解为可吸收的营养物质。相反，它会穿过消化系统，这有助于调节肠道蠕动。多项研究表明，某些类型的纤维可以降低胆固醇、帮助控制血糖水平并改善整体肠道健康。由于消化所需时间更长，它还能让你更长时间地感到饱腹。
世界卫生组织建议成年人每天摄入25-35克纤维。然而，泰莱公司在2021年至2022年间的研究显示，许多国家的成年人摄入量远未达到这一基准。美国国立卫生研究院告诉我们，女性的纤维摄入量低于男性。此外，世界卫生组织的数据显示出一个趋势：与居住在城市的人相比，居住在农村等非城市地区的人纤维摄入量较低。
研究发现，摄入纤维不足可能对你的健康产生不利影响。没有纤维，你的肠道细菌就无法抵抗过度炎症、提供能量，或管理你的血糖水平和情绪。身体上来说，你更容易便秘，感到无精打采和疲惫。
那么，你能做些什么呢？营养师建议每天吃五到八份水果和蔬菜。试着在咖喱、汤或沙拉中加入一把煮熟的扁豆或鹰嘴豆。你也可以在两餐之间吃种子、坚果和果干作为零食。目前谈论纤维可能感觉很时髦，但科学表明我们需要它来保持健康。所以，务必遵循营养师的建议，多吃水果和蔬菜！
